name: Slack (stealth)
description: Search Slack, read channels and threads, send messages, and add reactions using your browser session.

setup.title: Connect your Slack session
setup.description: Use your signed-in Slack browser session. No Slack app registration or OAuth client is required.
steps: Sign in to the Slack workspace you want to connect in your browser.
Use the upstream authentication guide to find the workspace's browser token (xoxc-) and its d session cookie (xoxd-). Enter them only in the secret fields below, never in chat.
Save the account settings and choose Connect. Wait for the account to show Connected, then check its available tools.
Test a small read, such as listing your channels. Messages and reactions act as your Slack user, within your account's access.

If Slack expires or revokes the session, replace both secret fields with credentials from your current session and reconnect. Stealth refers to app-free setup; Slack and workspace security systems can still observe activity.

fields.label: Slack browser token
fields.helpText: The browser token for this workspace, stored in your OpenTeam account settings.

fields.label: Slack session cookie
fields.helpText: The value of Slack's d cookie. Treat it as a login credential.

installationSteps: Open account settings and save your Slack browser token and session cookie in the secret fields.
Connect the account and verify a read tool returns data from the intended workspace.
Configure tool access in Accounts and settings. Add another account for each additional Slack workspace.
